skill.name: ui-handler
skill.description: Implement UI using Shadcn MCP (atoms/theme) and 21st.dev MCP (complex sections). Use when adding buttons, layouts, or generating landing pages.
skill.summary: Build consistent UI with Shadcn atoms, 21st.dev sections, Tailwind themes, and clear component placement.
skill.author: AayushBaniya2006

security_audit.summary: Static review found one confirmed command-execution risk: SKILL.md line 16 recommends pnpm dlx shadcn@latest as a manual fallback. The remaining static findings are Markdown path or import examples, and I found no prompt injection or malicious intent.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer Shadcn MCP, or pin the shadcn package version before running pnpm dlx. Require user confirmation for component names.

2.  **Compose**: Use atoms from `@/components/ui` and sections from `@/components/sections`.
3.  **Co-location**: If a component is unique to a page, put it in `_components/` next to the page.

finding_verdicts.reason: The `...` segment is an ellipsis placeholder in an architecture table, not a literal traversal token or file operation.

Line 16 instructs the agent to run `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add {component}` as a fallback. That executes a remote latest-tag package with a placeholder argument, so it is a real external-command risk.
Line 22 contains only documentation paths in Markdown code spans for where generated files should be placed. It does not invoke a shell or compose a command.
Line 23 names a page file in a Markdown code span. It is not shell execution or dynamic command construction.
Line 26 names a CSS file path in prose and permits direct editing. This is filesystem guidance, not an external command.
Line 29 shows Tailwind class and file examples inside Markdown code spans. It does not contain an executable command.
Line 33 lists import aliases and component directories in Markdown code spans. These are documentation references, not shell commands.
Line 34 shows a page-local component folder name. It is a placement convention and does not execute anything.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent UI changes without rebuilding common patterns. This skill guides Shadcn atoms, 21st.dev sections, theming, and page-level component placement.
actual_capabilities: Guides Shadcn MCP usage for buttons, inputs, dialogs, and other atoms.
Directs 21st.dev MCP prompts for landing pages, hero sections, and dashboards.
Defines component placement for atoms, shared sections, website files, and page-specific components.
Provides Tailwind theme guidance using CSS variables and OKLCH colors.
Encourages responsive layouts and semantic colors for dark mode support.
limitations: Depends on Shadcn MCP and 21st.dev MCP for the main workflow.
Does not include automated accessibility or performance validation.
The pnpm fallback runs a remote package and should be reviewed first.
Assumes a Next.js app structure with Tailwind conventions.

use_cases.title: Add Reusable UI Atoms
use_cases.description: Add standard interface elements while keeping component sources and file locations consistent.

use_cases.title: Generate Marketing Sections
use_cases.description: Create landing page heroes, footers, and dashboards from concise design direction.

use_cases.title: Organize Page Layouts
use_cases.description: Plan header, sidebar, content area, and page-specific components using clear placement rules.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-handler to add button and dialog components with Shadcn MCP. Keep styles aligned with the current theme.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Landing Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-handler to generate a responsive SaaS hero section with 21st.dev MCP. Place it in the shared sections area.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh The Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-handler to update the app theme with a neutral base, semantic color variables, and dark mode support.

prompt_templates.title: Compose A Full Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ui-handler to design a page layout with header, sidebar, content area, reusable atoms, and page-specific components.

output_examples.input: Add a modal workflow for user settings.
output: Shadcn dialog and form components are selected.
Reusable UI files remain in the shared component area.
The page integrates the modal through the project component path.

output_examples.output: A responsive hero section is generated through 21st.dev, reviewed for project style, and placed in the shared sections area.

output_examples.input: Refresh the theme for dark mode.
output: Theme variables are updated in the global stylesheet.
Semantic color names are preferred over hard-coded colors.
New UI elements inherit light and dark mode behavior.

best_practices: Use Shadcn MCP for atoms before writing custom component code.
Place reusable sections in shared directories and page-only pieces beside the page.
Review fallback commands and generated files before committing changes.
anti_patterns: Running the pnpm fallback without confirming the package source and component name.
Mixing hard-coded colors with semantic theme variables.
Putting one-off page components in shared directories without reuse.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build UI atoms, landing sections, themes, and layouts for Shadcn and Tailwind projects.

faq.question: Does it create components automatically?
faq.answer: It guides MCP tools that generate or add components. The agent still reviews and places the result.

faq.question: Do I need Shadcn installed?
faq.answer: The workflow assumes Shadcn and Tailwind conventions. Existing setup makes the guidance easier to apply.

faq.question: Does it support 21st.dev?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs 21st.dev Magic MCP for complex sections like heroes, dashboards, and landing pages.

faq.question: Is the pnpm fallback required?
faq.answer: No. Use it only when MCP is unavailable, and review the package version before running it.

faq.question: Is it limited to Next.js?
faq.answer: The paths target a Next.js app directory. Other React projects may need path adjustments.
